posts.author: flori9
posts.body:
GameJolt achievement plugin for RPG Maker MV
This plugin adds support for the GameJolt Achievement API to RPG Maker MV games. This API allows you to reward your players with online trophies and highscores that will show up on the GameJolt site and give your players EXP there. This is a great way to promote your game on GameJolt, as many people like games with trophies. Also, some players will play your game for longer as they want to get all trophies.
My aim is to make using this plugin as easy as possible, so that everybody can add online trophies and/or highscores to their games.
This plugin is still work in progress, but it's already useable. However, there may be bugs and some features will be added later.
Current features:
- Logging in to GameJolt. If the player is playing a web-based version on gamejolt.com, this will happen automatically. Otherwise, an easy-to-use login dialog will be shown.
- A button can be added to the main menu of the game to allow the user to log in and off.
- Sessions. This means you can see for how long your game is being played (by logged-in users). Also, a message will be shown on profiles of people that are playing your game.
- Trophies. You can easily give your players a trophy for doing something in-game. This will be displayed on the GameJolt site. The plugin also has support for showing basic trophy notifications. If a player is offline while reaching a trophy, the trophy will automatically be given the next time he/she is online.
- It's quite configurable. Please check out the help text for more information on what the different settings do.
Coming soon:
- Highscores.
- An example game.
- Possibly more if this is going to be used a bit. For example, I could add online save files or other data storage.
How to use:
Copy all files from the zip file and paste them into your plugin directory. Then enable the plugin and fill in the Game ID and Private Key in the plugin manager. They can be found on the dashboard page of your game on the GameJolt site. From the main dashboard page, go to the Game API tab. Then click on "API Settings" to the left. The Game ID and Private Key should be shown there. Copy them to the plugin parameters.
After you've entered these parameters, sessions will work automatically! You can use the following command to give a trophy:
GameJolt award trophy <id><id> is the ID of the trophy, which can be found on the Game API tab of your game dashboard on the "Trophies" tab after having added your trophy.
If you'd like more help, please click the help button in the plugin manager. If you still have a question then, feel free to post it below.
Licence:
Credits would be appreciated, but they're not required. If you do want to credit me, please use my name "Florian van Strien". I'm fine with this plugin being used commercially, but you'd have to talk to the GameJolt people if they'd be okay with a commercial game using their web services if you want to do so.
Download!
Learn more about the GameJolt Game API
Feedback is very welcome!

posts.author: flori9
posts.body:
@Ramiro:
I understand your concern and have thought about this as well. However, it's actually impossible to protect this well as everything is (and has to be) client side. I could, of course, encrypt the private key. However, that would make the plugin harder to use because you couldn't just input the private key in a plugin parameter anymore. It wouldn't actually increase security by much, too, as a hacker could just get hold of the private key after it has been decrypted (that has to be done somewhere, anyway). And even if they couldn't do that, they could still simply call
GameJolt.awardTrophy("<id>")
from the JavaScript console of the browser. And even if that wouldn't be possible in some magical way, they could change the game variable that impacts the score.
If you're concerned about this, I think the best you could do is running your whole project through a JavaScript compressor/obfuscator when it's done. That's still very much security through obscurity so it's totally not safe, but it might stop some people.
For highscores, I'll try to automatically add some extra information to each score so that it's a bit easier to detect and scores hacked scores.
Anyway, I think trophies and highscores are mostly just a bit of extra fun, so I don't think it is that's much of a problem if someone can hack them. Most people wouldn't do that anyway. Having a private key doesn't give anyone access to your account or something like that; and it's a per-game thing, so
it'll not make your GameJolt account or game page insecure
.
However, if you (or someone else) have(/has) any idea on how to protect the plugin some more, especially if that works without impacting ease-of-use, please do post here or send me a PM. I'd be very interested in your methods.

posts.author: flori9
posts.body:
I'm afraid I don't know much about security, so I'm not sure if they're using a public-private key pair or session token. I
think
the system is not nearly as advanced at that. Communicating with the servers basically works like this:
- I create a URI for the request I want to make. For example, this could be
h
ttp://gamejolt.com/api/game/v1/users/auth?game_id=103321&username=flori9&user_token=token&format=json
.
- I generate a MD5/SHA1 (I chose SHA1 here) hash of that URI plus a private key. For example, in this case I would generate a SHA1 of
h
ttp://gamejolt.com/api/game/v1/users/auth?game_id=103321&username=flori9&user_token=token&format=json0a836f26612f3f5108f1939162f14765
(where the private key is
0a836f26612f3f5108f1939162f14765
). This SHA1 would be
e619d2ca1726310007988298f2dd587eb4f084d2
.
- I append an extra parameter (named
signature
) to the URI with the generated hash. The full URI would be
h
ttp://gamejolt.com/api/game/v1/users/auth?game_id=103321&username=flori9&user_token=token&format=json&signature=e619d2ca1726310007988298f2dd587eb4f084d2
.
- I send off a GET request to this URI and receive a (unencrypted) response in JSON format. In this case, the response would be:
{"response":{"success":"false","message":"No such user with the credentials passed in could be found."}}
, as my user token isn't correct, but it would be
{"response":{"success":"true"}}
if it were. (The private key
is
correct, as I'm going to include it in the example game anyway.)
The only security element here is the private key. This key is hard-coded into the game. The user token is basically just an alternative for a password so that the user doesn't have to input their actual GameJolt password into games. This makes sure creators of games can't steal GameJolt passwords (and probably to make sure passwords aren't sent over insecure connections as well), but it doesn't add any security for the creator.
Please note that the engine is fully open source, so feel free to look at the code if you think something is unclear.
Edit:
By the way, to be clear, the private key is a per-game thing that's generated by GameJolt when you create the game. It can be found on the "dashboard" page of the game.
Edit 2:
Made URI's in the post fully readable. The automatic link converter on here is
agressive
, wow.

posts.author: Tsukihime
posts.body: Is there a particular reason why you've decided to hash the token?

posts.author: flori9
posts.body:
Yes, because that's the way the API works. I didn't design the URI format or server backend in any way, that's the work of GameJolts developers. If I wouldn't hash the URI + private key exactly this way the GameJolt API would simply deny all requests.
For the GJ API the idea basically is that GameJolt creates the backend while users make plugins/libraries for all the different languages and platforms. I'm just an user making such a plugin, I don't have any control over the backend.
